question: Why was my card declined when I tried to order, there's money in it?
expected_answer: Having funds isn't the only check: cards are often declined because the bank's fraud checks flag the payment, the Secure authentication step fails or times out, the billing address or postcode doesn't match the card, or a daily or online spending limit is hit, so it's worth checking with your bank.

key_facts: declines can come from the bank's fraud checks or a failed card authentication step
a billing address or postcode that doesn't match the card, or a spending limit, can also cause a decline

question: Do I need my receipt to get a refund on something I bought in store?
expected_answer: Not necessarily: an order confirmation email or a bank or card statement showing the purchase also counts, and the refund goes back to that card; with no proof of purchase at all you can only get an exchange or a gift card for the lowest price it sold for in the last 28 days, and you'll need photo ID.
answer_aliases: gift card at the lowest price in the last 28 days

key_facts: a bank or card statement showing the purchase counts as proof of purchase
with no proof of purchase: an exchange or a gift card for the lowest price the item sold for in the last 28 days
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, you need the original receipt; without it we can't give you a refund.

question: Is it a fault if I just don't like the colour of the kettle I got?
expected_answer: No, an item is only faulty if it isn't of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose or as described; not liking the colour is a change of mind, so it's handled as a normal return rather than a fault.
answer_aliases: change of mind, not a fault

key_facts: faulty means not of satisfactory quality, not fit for purpose or not as described
disliking the colour is a change of mind, not a fault

question: So can I return a coffee machine I've opened if it works fine?
expected_answer: Yes, within 14 days of purchase or delivery, but because it's opened and not faulty a restocking fee of 15% of the price is deducted from your refund, up to a maximum of £75, and it must be complete and undamaged.

key_facts: a restocking fee of 15% of the price is deducted from the refund
up to a maximum of £75
within 14 days of purchase or delivery
meta.common_prior: Yes, you can return it for a full refund within the returns period, usually 30 days, as long as it's in good condition with the packaging.

question: What's the return window on a laptop if I haven't even opened it?
expected_answer: You have 14 days from purchase or delivery, and because it's unopened with the factory seals intact you get a full refund to your original payment method.

key_facts: within 14 days of purchase or delivery
unopened items with factory seals intact get a full refund

question: What does click and collect mean, do I have to go in-store?
expected_answer: It means you order online and then pick the item up yourself from a store instead of having it delivered, so yes, you or someone collecting for you goes to the store to get it.
answer_aliases: order online, pick up in store

key_facts: you order online and collect from a store instead of having it delivered
someone has to go to the store to pick it up

question: How long will they keep it there before it goes back, then?
expected_answer: It's held for 3 days from the day the ready-to-collect message was sent; if it isn't collected by close of business on the 3rd day it's cancelled and refunded automatically, and the hold can't be extended.

history.text: Hi, I got a text saying my click and collect order is ready.
Lovely, I can see it's waiting at the store you picked.

key_facts: we hold your order for 3 days from the day we send the ready-to-collect message
uncollected orders are cancelled and refunded automatically
We can't extend the hold period
meta.common_prior: Orders are usually held for about 7 days, sometimes up to 14, before being sent back.

question: Can my son pick up my click and collect order for me?
expected_answer: Yes, with the collection code and order number if the order is under £500; for orders of £500 or more the collector must show photo ID matching the name on the order, unless you add him as a nominated collector in the app before it's ready, in which case he shows his own photo ID.
answer_aliases: yes, with the collection code and order number
photo ID for orders of £500 or more

key_facts: Anyone can collect with the collection code and order number for orders under £500
For orders of £500 or more, photo ID matching the name on the order, or a nominated collector added in the app before the order is ready
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, he just needs to show the collection code or your order confirmation email.

question: Does Saturday count as one of those working days, then?
expected_answer: No, working days are Monday to Friday, not counting weekends or bank holidays, so Saturday and Sunday don't count towards the three to five days.

history.text: I ordered a kettle and it said three to five working days.
Yes, it's on standard delivery and it left our warehouse on Thursday.

key_facts: working days are Monday to Friday
weekends and bank holidays don't count

question: Why didn't my order come next day? I placed it at nine pm.
expected_answer: Next-day delivery only applies if you order by 8 pm, Monday to Friday; an order placed after 8 pm misses that cutoff and goes out a working day later, and orders placed after 8 pm on Friday or at the weekend arrive on Tuesday.

key_facts: Order by 8 pm, Monday to Friday, for delivery on the next working day
Orders placed after 8 pm on Friday, or on Saturday or Sunday, arrive on Tuesday

question: How much is it to get a sofa delivered up to Inverness?
expected_answer: Sofas go by two-person delivery at £39 per order, plus a £30 surcharge for Highlands postcodes beginning IV like Inverness, so £69 in total, although two-person delivery itself is free on large-item orders over £1,000.

key_facts: two-person delivery is £39 per order
postcodes beginning IV carry a £30 surcharge on top of the £39 charge, £69 in total

question: What happens with nominated day delivery, do I get to pick the day?
expected_answer: Yes, that's what nominated day delivery is: you choose the specific date you want it delivered at checkout instead of taking the earliest available date.

key_facts: nominated day delivery means you choose the specific delivery date

question: My sofa's coming tomorrow, what happens if I move it to next week?
expected_answer: No, date changes are free only until 12 noon two working days before the delivery; with it due tomorrow, moving it costs a £25 rescheduling fee.

key_facts: change your delivery date free of charge until 12 noon two working days before the delivery
After that, a rescheduling fee of £25 applies
meta.common_prior: Yes, you can rearrange the delivery for free as long as you tell us before the day.

question: Right, so how many amps should the fuse for that plug be?
expected_answer: A washing machine plug takes a 13 amp fuse, the standard rating for high-power appliances; if the new fuse blows again, stop using the machine because that points to a fault.

history.text: The washing machine you delivered won't power on, and the plug fuse looks blown.
Sorry about that. You can swap the fuse yourself safely if it's the right rating.

key_facts: a washing machine needs a 13 amp fuse
a fuse that blows again suggests a fault

question: What does it cost to have you plumb in a new washing machine?
expected_answer: Standard installation is £45: the engineer connects it to existing water, waste and electrical points within 1 metre, removes the transit bolts and runs a short test cycle.

key_facts: standard installation is £45
connects the appliance to existing water, waste and electrical points within 1 metre

question: Uh, what happens to my old washing machine when you bring the new one?
expected_answer: We can take it away for £25 as a like-for-like swap when we deliver the new one, but it must already be disconnected and drained before the crew arrives, because they won't do that; if it isn't ready they can't take it and the fee is refunded.
answer_aliases: must be disconnected and drained first

key_facts: Removal and recycling of your old appliance: £25 per item
The old appliance must already be disconnected and drained before the crew arrives; the crew won't disconnect or drain it
meta.plausible_wrong_answer: Yes, the delivery crew will disconnect your old machine and take it away when they bring the new one.

question: How much is a fifty-five inch telly across, like is that the width?
expected_answer: No, TV sizes are measured diagonally across the screen from corner to corner, so a 55-inch TV is roughly 48 inches, about 122 cm, wide, plus a little for the frame.

key_facts: screen size is measured diagonally, corner to corner
a 55-inch TV is about 122 cm or 48 inches wide

question: What's the difference between wall mounting a sixty-five and a seventy-five inch TV?
expected_answer: Wall mounting is £99 for TVs up to 65 inches and £149 for 75 inches and above; the bracket isn't included in either price and must be suitable for your TV and wall.

key_facts: TV wall mounting: £99 for TVs up to 65 inches, and £149 for 75 inches and above
The bracket isn't included

question: What time are big stores like yours allowed to open on a Sunday?
expected_answer: Under Sunday trading law in England and Wales, large shops over 280 square metres can open for at most six consecutive hours on a Sunday, sometime between 10 am and 6 pm.
answer_aliases: six hours between 10 am and 6 pm

key_facts: Sunday trading rules limit large shops to six continuous hours
the hours must fall between 10 am and 6 pm

question: What time does the Cribbs Causeway store open on a Sunday morning?
expected_answer: The Cribbs Causeway store is open 10:30 am to 4:30 pm on Sundays.

key_facts: Sunday: 10:30 am to 4:30 pm

question: Is the Broadmead store open late on any night of the week?
expected_answer: Yes, Thursday is late-night opening at Broadmead, 9 am to 8 pm; on other days it closes at 6 pm, or 5 pm on Sundays.

key_facts: Thursday: 9 am to 8 pm (late-night opening)

question: What's the difference between the manufacturer's guarantee and an extended warranty?
expected_answer: The manufacturer's guarantee comes free with the product and covers manufacturing defects for a set period, honoured by the brand; an extended warranty is an optional paid plan, usually sold by the retailer or an insurer, that covers breakdowns for longer and sometimes extras like accidental damage.
answer_aliases: guarantee is free from the brand; extended warranty is paid

key_facts: the manufacturer's guarantee is free and covers defects for a set period
an extended warranty is an optional paid plan that extends cover

question: If I drop it, how much do I pay to claim?
expected_answer: A drop counts as accidental damage, which has an excess of £35 per claim, paid when the claim is approved; you can make up to 2 accidental damage claims in any 12 months.

history.text: I bought a laptop last month with the Care Complete plan.
Thanks, yes, I can see the plan is active on your account.

key_facts: Each accidental damage claim has an excess of £35
up to 2 accidental damage claims in any 12 months

question: Um, how come the same TV has another model number at other shops?
expected_answer: Manufacturers often make slightly different versions of the same TV for different retailers, changing a feature, accessory or finish and giving each a unique model number, which also makes direct price comparison harder.

key_facts: manufacturers make retailer-specific variants with their own model numbers
this makes direct price comparison harder

question: Can I still get the price match if I'm not signed up to anything?
expected_answer: No, the Price Promise is now only for Hearth Rewards members, but membership is free and you can join in store, online or by phone before you claim, even on the same day.

key_facts: the Price Promise is now available only to Hearth Rewards members
Membership is free and you can join before you make a claim, even on the same day
meta.common_prior: Yes, price matching is open to every customer; just show us the competitor's price.

question: If I find it cheaper after buying, how soon should I claim the difference?
expected_answer: You can claim within 14 days of purchase, and the difference is refunded to your original payment method within 5 working days, as long as it's the identical product at a UK retailer with at least 10 physical stores.

key_facts: within 14 days of purchase
refund the difference to your original payment method within 5 working days

question: With nought percent APR, is there any interest charge on top of the sofa price?
expected_answer: No, nought percent APR means no interest is charged, so you repay only the cash price of the sofa spread over the agreed months, as long as you make every payment as agreed.

key_facts: no interest is charged
you repay only the cash price spread over the term

question: Why doesn't the finance option show up when my basket's quite small?
expected_answer: Interest-free finance is only available on orders of £399 or more, so the option only appears at checkout once your basket reaches £399; smaller baskets from £50 can use Pay in 3 instead.

key_facts: Interest-free finance: on orders of £399 or more
The finance option only appears at checkout once your basket reaches £399

question: How long is a king-size bed compared to the double I've got?
expected_answer: In the UK a standard double is 190 cm long and 135 cm wide, and a king-size is 200 cm long and 150 cm wide, so a king is about 10 cm longer.

key_facts: a UK king-size bed is 200 cm long and a double is 190 cm long

question: What does made-to-order mean for cancelling my sofa, how long have I got?
expected_answer: Made-to-order sofas can be cancelled free of charge only within 48 hours of placing the order; after that production has started and a cancellation charge of 25% of the price applies, and they can't be returned once delivered unless faulty.

key_facts: You can cancel a made-to-order item free of charge within 48 hours of placing the order
a cancellation charge of 25% of the item price applies after 48 hours
meta.common_prior: You have a 14-day cooling-off period to cancel an order for a full refund.
